items.toString:
h2. Summary

  The ODF must-gather should collect OperatorGroup resources to provide complete OLM troubleshooting information.

h2. Description

  Currently, the ODF must-gather collects several OLM (Operator Lifecycle Manager) resources including:

* Subscriptions
* ClusterServiceVersions (CSVs)
* CatalogSources
* InstallPlans
* OperatorConditions

  However, it does not collect OperatorGroup resources, which are a critical component of OLM that defines the target namespaces for operator
  installation and the namespaces an operator should watch.

h2. Business Case / Justification

  OperatorGroups are essential for troubleshooting operator installation and configuration issues:

# *Installation failures*: Incorrect or missing OperatorGroup configurations are a common cause of operator installation failures
# *Namespace watching issues*: OperatorGroups define which namespaces an operator watches, critical for multi-namespace deployments
# *Complete OLM context*: Without OperatorGroup information, support engineers and developers have an incomplete view of the OLM configuration when analysing must-gather data
# *Debugging operator behavior*: Issues related to operator scope (AllNamespaces vs OwnNamespace vs SingleNamespace) cannot be properly diagnosed without OperatorGroup details

h2. Current Behavior

  OperatorGroup resources are not collected by the must-gather, requiring manual collection when troubleshooting operator-related issues.

h2. Desired Behavior

  The must-gather should automatically collect OperatorGroup resources in the operator namespace(s), similar to how it collects other OLM resources.

h2. Proposed Implementation

Add {{operatorgroup}} to the collection commands in {{collection-scripts/gather_namespaced_resources}}:

For  {{oc get}} output (around line 29):

{code:bash}commands_get+=("operatorgroup")

For oc describe output (around line 50):
commands_desc+=("operatorgroup")

For YAML output (around line 66):
oc_yamls+=("operatorgroup")
{code}

# *Outline the proposed title of this feature request.*
Forced OSD Removal Fail-Safe
# *What is the nature and problem description of the request?*
Currently our [docs|https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_data_foundation/4.21/html/replacing_devices/openshift_data_foundation_deployed_using_local_storage_devices#replacing-operational-or-failed-storage-devices-on-clusters-backed-by-local-storage-devices_rhodf] have an excerpt on how to remove osd's in 3 node clusters

{noformat}The FORCE_OSD_REMOVAL value must be changed to “true” in clusters that only have three OSDs, or clusters with insufficient space to restore all three replicas of the data after the OSD is removed.{noformat}

     We had a customer recently that used the “FORCE_OSD_REMOVAL=true” flag sequentially across  osd’s that reside in different failure domains (04463436). The result was data loss.

My proposal is that we add a second fail-safe to the osd removal process since our customers have a fairly easy-to-pull, and very public lever to shoot themselves in the foot with the “FORCE_OSD_REMOVAL=true” flag. 

Preferably this added fail-safe is not just another flag appended onto the “oc process ocs-osd-removal” job, but something more complex to implement. A config-map change that green-lights osd forced removals would even work. 

I also think we should be more verbose about what the “FORCE_OSD_REMOVAL=true” does. Warnings about the potential for data loss in our osd removal job’s pod logs and/or our documentation would prudent in my opinion.

# *Why does the customer need this? (List the business requirements here)*
So they don’t remove osd’s in a way that causes data loss.
# *Are there any Documentation Requirements for this request?*
No, not if we want to hide this feature from customers.
# *Is the request coming from a specific customer or subset of customers (on prem only, cloud only, etc). Please don't mention any customer related sensitive information.*
No.
# *What is the urgency of the request?*
Non-Urgent
# *Please provide contact information, in case of follow up questions.*
bmcmurra@redhat.com - Email
bmcmurra -Slack

*1. Proposed Title of Feature Request*
*Enable Configurable Resource Requests and Limits for the OSD Log-Collector Container to Support Guaranteed QoS*

*2. Nature and Description of the Request*
*Context:*
In OpenShift Data Foundation (ODF), Object Storage Daemon (OSD) pods typically run two primary containers: the main OSD container and the log-collector container. While upstream Rook-Ceph supports configuring resource requests and limits for the log-collector container, this capability is currently missing or inaccessible in ODF.

*The Problem:*
Currently, there is no mechanism to explicitly define CPU and memory requests and limits for the log-collector container. In Kubernetes, a pod can only achieve a Guaranteed Quality of Service (QoS) class if every container within the pod (including init and sidecar containers) has CPU and memory requests that strictly equal their respective limits. Because the log-collector lacks these configurable parameters, OSD pods are forced into a Burstable QoS class.

*The Impact:*
OSDs are critical, latency-sensitive infrastructure components. Forcing them to run with a Burstable QoS class is highly problematic. It subjects the storage layer to CPU contention and makes OSD pods susceptible to eviction during node resource pressure. Furthermore, running in a Burstable state prevents the effective use of advanced performance-tuning configurations, such as enforcing single-NUMA node policies on multi-NUMA servers.

*Proposed Solutions:*

Primary Recommendation: Expose configuration parameters within the ODF operator to allow administrators to manually define CPU and memory requests and limits for the log-collector container, achieving feature parity with upstream Rook-Ceph.

*Alternative Recommendation:* If exposing these settings is not viable, implement intelligently calculated or static, hard-coded default values for the log-collector container where requests are strictly equal to limits. As long as these values fulfill the Kubernetes requirements for Guaranteed QoS without starving the log-collector process, this approach is acceptable.

*3. Business Requirements*
*Predictable and Maximal Performance:* Enable Guaranteed QoS for OSD pods to ensure stable, high-throughput, and low-latency storage performance.

*Infrastructure Reliability:* Prevent critical storage components from competing for CPU resources with noisy neighbors or being preempted/evicted during cluster resource constraints.

*Hardware Optimization:* Unlock the ability to fully leverage multi-NUMA server architectures through proper resource pinning and allocation.

*4. Affected Packages or Components*
OpenShift Data Foundation (ODF)

# *Outline the proposed title of this feature request.*
Allow use of xattr to be switched off
 # *What is the nature and problem description of the request?*
Currently a NFS based PV requires the underlying provider supports xattr. The request is for the use of xattr to be switched off using an environment variable SKIP_REPLACE_XATTR
 # *Why does the customer need this? (List the business requirements here)*
The customer (Lloyds Banking Group) has extensively tested using a PV Pool type setup but is constrained by the use of the Postgres database for S3 metadata. Instead, ODF engineering have recommended using a NSFS type configuration using a PV which does not rely on the PostGres database and will deliver an improved performance. 

The customer uses Portworx to provide storage which does not currently support the use of xattr with the sharedv4 service storage class since it uses NFS version 4 and xattr is only implemented with NFS 4.2. 

The related support case is: [https://access.redhat.com/support/cases/#/case/04115361/related-tasks] 

Work has started on this enhancement as part of https://issues.redhat.com/browse/DFBUGS-2955 

This RFE is being raised so that the work can continue in this ticket and follow a non-bug type workflow
 # *Are there any Documentation Requirements for this request?*
Yes, the drawbacks of not using xattr need to be documented for the customer in our public facing documentation along with how it can be switched off using the environment variable
 # *Is the request coming from a specific customer or subset of customers (on prem only, cloud only, etc). Please don't mention any customer related sensitive information.*
Lloyds Banking Group are making the request
 # *What is the urgency of the request?*
Medium
 # *Please provide contact information, in case of follow up questions.*
Mark Pearson - [marpears@redhat.com|mailto:marpears@redhat.com]
Tony Scully - [tscully@redhat.com|mailto:tscully@redhat.com] 
Steve Mulholland - [smullhol@redhat.com|mailto:smullhol@redhat.com]

# *Outline the proposed title of this feature request.*
ODF should avoid logging debug logs in default deployment on all components
 # *What is the nature and problem description of the request?*
Debug logs are often for deep dives in development / engineering scenarios and are mostly not intended for production use cases. However, the default deployment of ODF does have debug logs enabled in several components. The following commands can be used to determine the existing debug logs from a ODF must-gather: 
{code:java}
# files with debug logs $ find . -type f -name "*.log" -exec grep -i "debug" {} + > ../files_including_debug_logs.out 

# Just the files $ find . -type f -name "*.log" -exec grep -il "debug" {} + | uniq > ../files_with_debug_logs.out 

# files with logs and proper separaters$ cat ../files_with_debug_logs.out| while read -r line; do echo "\n\n\n====================================================================\n file $line \n====================================================================\n"; grep "$line" ../files_including_debug_logs.out; done > ../files_and_log_lines_separated_with_new_lines.out
{code}
The above output led to the identification of the following components to log debug logs:
Deployments:

 * rook-ceph-mon-a
 * rook-ceph-mon-b
 * rook-ceph-mon-c
 * ceph-csi-controller-manager
 * openshift-storage.rbd.csi.ceph.com-ctrlplugin
 * openshift-storage.cephfs.csi.ceph.com-ctrlplugin
 * rook-ceph-mgr-a
 * rook-ceph-mgr-b
 * rook-ceph-rgw-ocs-storagecluster-cephobjectstore-a
 * rook-ceph-mds-ocs-storagecluster-cephfilesystem-a
 * rook-ceph-mds-ocs-storagecluster-cephfilesystem-b
 * rook-ceph-osd-*
 * odf-operator-controller-manager
 * csi-addons-controller-manager
 * noobaa-operator

       Daemonsets:
 * openshift-storage.rbd.csi.ceph.com-nodeplugin-csi-addons

Should today's debug logging be required to deliver support for customers, then please change them to info/warning/error. Should those logs not be required, then please remove them by increasing the log level. The intention is NOT to break the customer experience on support delivery.
 # *Why does the customer need this? (List the business requirements here)*
Debug logs should not be enabled in production scenarios. 
Debug logs on all components cannot be turned of, as of today.
 # *Are there any Documentation Requirements for this request?*
No
 # *Is the request coming from a specific customer or subset of customers (on prem only, cloud only, etc). Please don't mention any customer related sensitive information.*
On Prem
 # *What is the urgency of the request?*
Not urgent, normal
 # *Please provide contact information, in case of follow up questions.*
See reporter and Jira comments.

# *Outline the proposed title of this feature request.*
The proposal is to add features to odf-cli to make working with cephfs volumes (especially cleanup operations) much easier. 

 # *What is the nature and problem description of the request?*
It is very hard to actually get a clear picture about CephFS snapshots, pending clones, clones in process, subvolumes. Cleanup of pending clones and in-process clones is also not easy to do as it involves a lot of CLI fiddling to get the right outputs.

 # *Why does the customer need this? (List the business requirements here)*
It takes quite a long time to cleanup clones, volumes, snapshots, especially on external ceph clusters with multiple ODF clusters attached to it.

I created a script which is downloadable in KCS [1] which did help us *a lot* in multiple cases to make cleanup processes more efficient. Especially an easy way to create a report for `snapshots`, `clones`, `subvolumes` is currently missing. Even if you cleanup a snapshot, or a clone, or subvolume, to get a list it's a lot of CLI work, with the script from [1] it's very easy to get a nice report which is quick to generate.
 
 # *Are there any Documentation Requirements for this request?*
Documentation of potentially new odf-cli commands

 # *Is the request coming from a specific customer or subset of customers (on prem only, cloud only, etc). Please don't mention any customer related sensitive information.*
No, it's a general issue

 # *What is the urgency of the request?*
There is no urgency, we are just loosing a lot of time guiding CU's to run the right commands to execute to get information which should be much easier to obtain.

 # *Please provide contact information, in case of follow up questions.*
 You can followup with rsachere@redhat.com 

I open this RFE because after talking with Lijo he saw a benefit of actually have this script or script functionality in odf-cli. I looked over the odf-cli code and I am pretty sure the functionality is rather easy to implement. 

[1] https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7080701

items.toString: [RDR] Error messages from VR and VRG yaml aren't reciprocating in the DRPC yaml

Created from https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHSTOR-6638

Ramen propagates VR conditions error messages in the VRG protected pvcs conditions.  Ramen summarizes the VR conditions into VRG and later DRPC, which currently does not reflect per PVC message, and is more a summary. Ramen may want to look at how best to bubble up the message, or leave it at VRG layer for easier troubleshooting and user feedback.

We need to discuss what and how we want to expose on the DRPC - can be the entire protected pvcs list, or maybe list of errors. Maybe better to split this work to another task, since the first part should be ready now.

items.toString: [RFE][GSS] Add Prometheus metrics about IO/s bandwith and IO latency on each PV and object bucket backed by ODF

items.fromString:
Say for example you have a cluster with a workload of 500 clients on 300 cephfs volumes. Using the below promql quey an observed total bandwidth consumption of 500 Mb/s is returned. 

sum by (name) (rate(ceph_pool_wr_bytes[5m]) * on (pool_id) group_left(name) ceph_pool_metadata\{name=~"ocs-storagecluster-cephfilesystem-data0"})

Before 4.16, there is no way to know; the per-client metricsceph_mds_client_metrics_ocs_storagecluster* do not exist. Since 4.16, per-client metrics are available: you have the consumption per client, but you have no way of knowing which pods are hiding behind each clientID.


Requested solution:
Add a metric that provides this information. for example:

ceph_mds_client_info\{client="client.8675309", ip_addr="10.10.10.10", subvol="csi-vol-0db1a72c-6589-4e98-877b-e602a872b7f4", hostname="nameisbetty.afundomain.com", ...}

# *Outline the proposed title of this feature request.*
Enable label matching prefix in BucketClass for controlled bucket tagging with OBC labels.


 # *What is the nature and problem description of the request?*
Currently, users can add any labels to an Object Bucket Claim (OBC), and all labels except: \{"app", "noobaa-domain", "bucket-provisioner"} are updated as bucket tagging. This unrestricted labels to tags conversion can lead to unintended tagging.
So, we should support a feature that allows specifying a matching label prefix in the BucketClass so that only the labels in the OBC that matches the label prefix in the BucketClass are updated as bucket tagging.
Example: `bucket-tags-label-prefix: noobaa.bucket.tags/` (an additional parameter in BucketClass)

It can be helpful in prevent unintentional bucket tagging.

Yes to make the customers aware of this feature.

No

Not so urgent but will be helpful for customers.

# {*}Outline the proposed title of this feature request.{*}{*}{*}

Add client side information to identify ceph IO, like pod UUID, workload, like throughput, block size, IOs, filesystem pod consumption.
 # *What is the nature and problem description of the request?*
At this moment, we can not show the top ten client pods consumers of a cephfs volume. 
We can not set alerts to avoid cephfs disruption, because some pods are exhausting the cephfs band width or configuring QoS to distribute or prioritize the IOs among the client pods.
 # *Why does the customer need this? (List the business requirements here)*
To prevent ODF outages because of IO bottlenecks caused by noisy pods.
 # *Are there any Documentation Requirements for this request?*
No
 # *Is the request coming from a specific customer or subset of customers (on prem only, cloud only, etc). Please don't mention any customer related sensitive information.*
Became from a great customer which is Inditex.

 # *What is the urgency of the request?*
High at this moment they are "blind" about what pods are top consumers and they suffered a Cephfs outage. 
 # *Please provide contact information, in case of follow up questions.*
TAM customer:  José Enrique Gutiérrez Mazón
CSE customer:  Mikel Olasagasti

# *Outline the proposed title of this feature request.* **

Ability to add multiple interfaces for OSD Cluster network via ODF CEPH Rook and setting OSD PODs to QoS guaranteed to attain the proper NUMA allocation (OSD pods in the same NUMA zone as the disks).
 #  *What is the nature and problem description of the request?*

Rook CEPH currently can only use 1 NAD and not multiple NADs. Customer needs to define multiple NADs based on 2 SR-IOV VFs and a Linux Bond on top of them to form the cluster network. Rook CEPH is unable to handle more than 1 NAD to define the CEPH cluster connection. Customer also needs the OSD PODS to be POD QoS Guaranteed.

 
 # *Why does the customer need this? (List the business requirements here)*

Customer's requirement is to achieve NUMA alignment of OSDs to be close to NVMe disks used as LocalVolumes from the OSD container. 

Customer is proposing to tune CEPH OSD PODs (and especially CEPH OSD Containers) to run on NUMA 1 node (Second CPU) and using SR-IOV VF- BOND for OSD Clustering network connection via Ceph Rook. The specific solution would require to:

1) use SRIOV NADs and Bond interface for CEPH Cluster network connection to use Device Manager hints to align into the right NUMA node. SR-IOV requires 2 NADs to be predefined and included in the ocs-cluster.

2) modify OSD Pods QoS class to have PoD QoS Guaranteed. This will use CPU Manager hints to align OSD Pods into the right NUMA node.
 

The hints in 1) and 2) will provide Topology Manager to make the desired NUMA-1 allocation in the proper vCPUs possible.

       1. *Are there any Documentation Requirements for this request?*
 # *Is the request coming from a specific customer or subset of customers (on prem only, cloud only, etc). Please don't mention any customer related sensitive information.*

On-prem deployment with ODF running in internal model.
 # {*}What is the urgency of the request?{*}{*}{{*}}

Feature requested by OCP 4.20.
 # {*}Please provide contact information, in case of follow up questions.{*}{*}{{*}}

           **          Jose Nunez (Red Hat)

 #  *What is the nature and problem description of the request?*

Rook CEPH currently can only use 1 NAD and not multiple NADs. Customer needs to define multiple NADs based on 2 SR-IOV VFs and a Linux Bond on top of them to form the cluster network. Rook CEPH is unable to handle more than 1 NAD to define the CEPH cluster connection. Customer also needs the OSD PODS to be POD QoS Guaranteed.

 
 # *Why does the customer need this? (List the business requirements here)*

Nokia NCP Blueprint (Class B on ECi deployment) design requires to tune CEPH OSD PODs and especially CEPH OSD Container to run on NUMA 1 node (Second CPU) and using SR-IOV VF- BOND for OSD Clustering network connection. Customer needs to

1) use SRIOV NADs and Bond interface for CEPH Cluster network connection to use Device Manager hints to align into the right NUMA node. SR-IOV requires 2 NADs to be predefined and included in the ocs-cluster.

2) modify OSD Pods QoS class to have PoD QoS Guaranteed. This will use CPU Manager hints to align OSD Pods into the right NUMA node.
 

The hints in 1) and 2) will provide Topology Manager to make the desired NUMA-1 allocation in the proper vCPUs possible.
